SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.20  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (i) a strong C≡N stretching band at 2281 cm⁻¹, characteristic of an aliphatic nitrile, (ii) a broad O–H/N–H stretch near 3200 cm⁻¹ indicating one hydroxyl (or possible secondary amine) group, (iii) intense aliphatic C–H stretches at 3002, 2956, 2913 and 2862 cm⁻¹, (iv) a strong C–O stretch around 1024 cm⁻¹, and (v) typical CH₃/CH₂ bending modes at 1466, 1445 and 1306 cm⁻¹.  
Among the candidates, only molecule 1 (CC(O)(C#N)CO) contains exactly one nitrile and a hydroxyl attached to a tert-butyl–like aliphatic framework, perfectly matching the observed CN, OH and aliphatic features. Candidates lacking either –OH or –C≡N (6, 8, 10) or containing multiple nitriles (9) or additional ring/heteroatom signatures inconsistent with the spectrum are less compatible. Therefore candidate 1 best fits the experimental Raman data despite the unexplained 2384 cm⁻¹ band.
